t: Introduction to Religions (Two from: Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Sikhism, Baha'i, Jainism, Taoism, Indigenous Religions)
Internal Assessment: Investigative Study of a Religious Practice

introduction-to-religions-two-from-buddh: Nine religions, three questions: how can you study a faith that is not your own fairly?
internal-assessment-investigative-study-: You have 1,800 words to study one living religious practice. How do you choose a question worth asking?
buddhism: Buddhists "take refuge" every day. What are they sheltering from, and where do they go?
buddhism-part-2: A prince starved himself almost to death, then ate a bowl of rice. Why was that the turning point?
christianity: When Christians share bread and wine, what do they believe they are really receiving?
christianity-part-2: Doctors sometimes bring back the dead. Is that what Christians mean by Jesus' resurrection?
christianity-part-3: Can a painting, a song or a string of beads bring someone closer to God?
hinduism: In Hindu worship, why does seeing the deity matter, and being seen by it matter just as much?
hinduism-part-2: How can Hindus say God is beyond every word and also worship God with flowers in a temple?
hinduism-part-3: What holds the world together, and why do Hindus say it is slowly wearing away?
introduction-world-religions-part-2: If humans are made in God's image, why do Christians say everyone needs saving?
islam: Muslims pray at set times, in set words, facing one place. Is there room left for the heart?
islam-part-2: A message says "the Prophet said…". How do Muslims decide whether he really said it?
islam-part-3: Why would a Muslim who already prays five times a day choose a teacher and a path of training?
judaism: Why would someone choose not to switch on a light for 25 hours every week?
judaism-part-2: If God has no body, why does the Torah talk about God's hand, eyes and voice?
judaism-part-3: Why do Jews pray the same words three times a day, and why is the best gift a job?
sikhism: Any building can become a gurdwara. What turns it into one, and why does everyone eat there?
sikhism-part-2: If your actions decide your next life, how can a gift from God set you free?

introduction-to-religions-two-from-buddh: Nine religions, three questions: how can you study a faith that is not your own fairly?
If you have lived many times before, what are you trying to escape, and how?
If nothing lasts and there is no fixed "you", what does it mean to be set free?
What if the biggest thing standing between you and God is the word "I"?
If a spark of God lives in everyone, why do so many people act selfishly?
If every person has an urge to do wrong, why did the rabbis say that urge can also build a house?
internal-assessment-investigative-study-: You have 1,800 words to study one living religious practice. How do you choose a question worth asking?
Your interviews are done. How do you turn what people told you into real analysis?
buddhism: Buddhists "take refuge" every day. What are they sheltering from, and where do they go?
Why would Buddhists bow to a statue and give gifts, if the Buddha cannot receive them?
The Buddha wrote nothing down. How do Buddhists know what he taught?
If a father lies to get his children out of a burning house, has he done wrong?
Why did the Buddha's first sermon sound like a doctor's diagnosis?
If a chariot is only its parts, is there anyone inside you doing the steering?
If the Buddhist goal is beyond words, how can anyone aim for it?
buddhism-part-2: A prince starved himself almost to death, then ate a bowl of rice. Why was that the turning point?
Buddhists keep precepts that no god commands. So what happens when one is broken?
The Eightfold Path has eight parts. Is it a ladder you climb, or something else?
Can sitting still and calming the mind be a step towards awakening, or only a pleasant rest?
Can watching your own breath and itches show you the truth about who you are?
Pali texts show the Buddha eating meat he was given. So must a Buddhist be vegetarian to avoid harm?
A soldier asked the Buddha if warriors who die in battle go to heaven. Why did he refuse to answer?
christianity: When Christians share bread and wine, what do they believe they are really receiving?
Why do some churches share bread every day and others only once a month?
Should a baby be baptised before it can choose, or should baptism wait until a person can say yes?
Why do some Christians celebrate Christmas on 7 January, and Easter weeks after their neighbours?
Christians call the Bible God's word, yet human hands wrote and chose every book. How can both be true?
A book finished nearly 2,000 years ago: how do Christians get advice from it for life today?
christianity-part-2: Doctors sometimes bring back the dead. Is that what Christians mean by Jesus' resurrection?
Was Jesus fully God, or the first and greatest thing God made? Why did it matter so much?
Christians pray to Father, Son and Holy Spirit. How can that still be one God?
If Christians will rise from the dead, will they get back the same body, or a new kind?
How did a small prayer meeting in Los Angeles become a quarter of world Christianity?
christianity-part-3: Can a painting, a song or a string of beads bring someone closer to God?
When Christians decide what is right, does the Bible decide, or the Church, reason, or love?
Christians say love is the root of every value. Where does that love come from, and what does it ask?
"Blessed are you who are poor": did Jesus really mean that literally?
In Jesus' most famous stories, why is the hero so often the person nobody expected?
hinduism: In Hindu worship, why does seeing the deity matter, and being seen by it matter just as much?
Why do Hindus light bonfires and throw colours at Holi, and welcome a warrior goddess home each autumn?
Can a river wash away wrongdoing, and can a holy place exist outside India?
Hindus say some scriptures were "heard" and others "remembered". Why does the difference matter?
A boy asks Death what happens after we die. What does Death teach him about the self?
A warrior refuses to fight his own family. Why does his charioteer Krishna tell him to stand up?
hinduism-part-2: How can Hindus say God is beyond every word and also worship God with flowers in a temple?
Is your deepest self a tiny part of God, a separate soul, or God itself in disguise?
If you can't remember your past lives, how can you be paying for what you did in them?
A thinker, a worker and a lover of God: can they all reach the same goal by different roads?
How did poems sung in Tamil, Marathi and Hindi let outcastes and women reach God directly?
Millions do yoga in gyms. Is that the same yoga Hindu teachers practised to win liberation?
hinduism-part-3: What holds the world together, and why do Hindus say it is slowly wearing away?
An ancient hymn pictures society as one body. Does it make caste sacred?
Must a Hindu's life follow four set stages, and can love of God break the rules?
Is it possible to live without harming anything at all, even an insect or an embryo?
Krishna tells Arjuna to fight; Gandhi called the same book his guide to non-violence. How?
introduction-world-religions-part-2: If humans are made in God's image, why do Christians say everyone needs saving?
If Muslims say people are born good, why does everyone still need a path to follow?
Why would a religion teach that the best way to act is often to stop forcing things?
Jains worship no creator god, yet bow before 24 perfect teachers. What are they trying to become?
How can one faith honour Moses, the Buddha, Jesus and Muhammad, yet say a new messenger came after them?
islam: Muslims pray at set times, in set words, facing one place. Is there room left for the heart?
Why do pilgrims at Makkah dress so simply and alike, and what changed when pilgrims began to fly?
What can an empty stomach teach that a full one cannot?
If the Qur'an came in pieces over 23 years, how did it become one book?
Why do Muslims who don't speak Arabic still learn to recite the Qur'an in Arabic?
islam-part-2: A message says "the Prophet said…". How do Muslims decide whether he really said it?
Muslims say nothing is like God, yet call God by ninety-nine names. How can both be true?
If God sent many prophets and books before Muhammad, why do Muslims need the Qur'an?
Muslims honour Abraham, Moses and Jesus. So why is Muhammad called the "seal" of the prophets?
Muslims believe the dead wait, rise and are judged. What happens at each stage, and why does it matter now?
islam-part-3: Why would a Muslim who already prays five times a day choose a teacher and a path of training?
A Sufi cried out "I am the Real" and was executed. What did he mean, and what do Sufis say of God?
The Qur'an never mentions cocaine. How do Muslim scholars know it is forbidden?
Islam has five verdicts for any action, not two. Why would a religion need a "disliked" category?
Why do Muslims call the fight against your own selfishness the "greater" jihad?
judaism: Why would someone choose not to switch on a light for 25 hours every week?
Why does a Jewish family retell the same escape story at the same meal every year?
Why do Jews blow a ram's horn, then fast for 25 hours ten days later?
Is the Torah God's own words, or human words inspired by God?
If the Torah was written down, why do Jews say Moses also received a Torah by word of mouth?
Jews believe in one God who has no body. So how can anyone say what God is like?
judaism-part-2: If God has no body, why does the Torah talk about God's hand, eyes and voice?
Maimonides listed beliefs every Jew must hold. Why did other great rabbis argue with his list?
How would Jews know the Messiah had come? What would the world look like?
Some Jewish mystics say a soul can return to finish unfinished work. Where does that idea come from?
Can dancing and singing bring you closer to God than years of study?
judaism-part-3: Why do Jews pray the same words three times a day, and why is the best gift a job?
If the Torah holds 613 commandments, why did only ten go on the stone tablets?
Why does a book of Jewish law contain a chapter of advice on how to be a good person?
Jewish law says break Shabbat to save a life. Could it ever allow weapons that kill millions?
Can a few cells in a dish, which could never grow into a baby there, be used to save lives?
sikhism: Any building can become a gurdwara. What turns it into one, and why does everyone eat there?
If two people are both Sikhs, why might only one of them wear a steel bangle, comb and sword?
Why do Sikhs light up the Golden Temple for a prisoner's release, and mark New Year with a call for a head?
Who wrote the Sikh scripture, and why do scholars argue about how it was put together?
Sikhs treat a book as their living Guru. What does that mean, and is it worship?
Why do Sikhs start each day with a poem that says God cannot be grasped by thinking?
Can a God "without qualities" also be a friend, a mother and a king?
sikhism-part-2: If your actions decide your next life, how can a gift from God set you free?
If everything happens by God's will, does a Sikh's own effort make any difference?
How can repeating one word over and over change the person who says it?
Why would a religion that seeks union with God insist that you go out and earn a living?
Why would Sikhs say that washing dishes in a gurdwara kitchen can bring them closer to God?
Why did a Guru who taught peace and meditation start wearing two swords?
